title: Walk Time: Looking ahead after IAAPA
summary:
By Robert Niles: "Walk Time" is Theme Park Insider's Saturday look back at theme park news from the past week.

The 2027 IAAPA Expo wrapped yesterday, after welcoming 45,580 registered attendees for the association's largest event ever. The sow floor expanded by 50% as IAAPA took over the Orange County Convention Center's West building in addition to the North/South facility. During the week, we got news and updates about several projects coming to major parks and destinations. Here is a recap of our coverage:

  • Mattel expands its Arizona theme park plans
  • IAAPA opens record Expo show floor in Orlando (includes coaster reveals from Six Flags, Herschend, Lagoon, and Holiday World)
  • Here are the winners of the 2027 Thea Awards
  • Busch Gardens is getting a new water coaster for 2027, too
  • United Parks offers fresh looks at what's next in 2027
  • Could Kennedy Space Center become a major theme park destination?

Hours before the IAAPA Expo show floor opened, Disney reported its latest quarterly and annual earnings. The company reported record attendance at its destinations over the past year, showing once again that it remains the industry undisputed commercial leader. Disney reports all-time record in guest attendance in 2026.

So of course we had to talk about that on this week' Theme Park Insider Podcast - Podcast: Why no one can catch Disney.

Universal should see a boost in attendance following its decision to open its new Epic Universe theme park to annual passholders. But there are a couple of catches: you'll have to buy an upgraded pass that includes Epic and you'll need to make advance park reservations to use it there. Get the details at Universal Orlando to open Epic Universal to annual passes.

Finally, check out this week's U.S. patent application finds:

  • Universal files plan for self-fixing theme park attraction
  • Disney has a plan to make moving chocolate treats

Thank you, as always, for reading Theme Park Insider, contributing to our discussions, and for sharing our links!

title: Holiday celebrations start at Knott's, Universal, and Six Flags
summary:
By Robert Niles: More holiday events are opening this weekend, as Christmas celebrations continue at theme parks across America.

Tonight is the opening for the return of Knott's Merry Farm at Knott's Berry Farm in California. The park this year is opening an all-new Snoopy's Merry Christmas Follies ice show in the Walter Knott Theater, joining the returning The Gift of the Magi 1885 and A Calico Christmas Carol in the Bird Cage Theatre, Home for the Holidays on the Calico Mine Stage, Calico Carolers in Ghost Town, Santa's Christmas Cabin, and the nightly Tis the Season Tree Lighting Ceremony in Calico Park.

Up the road at Universal Studios Hollywood, the park's Holidays celebration starts Saturday, with the returns of Grinchmas at Who-ville in Universal Plaza and Christmas in The Wizarding World of Harry Potter. Universal also is serving new holiday-themed food throughout the park, including at The Three Broomsticks, Minion Cafe, and Toadstool Cafe.

Across the country, Six Flags Great Adventure is previewing its 2027 Holiday in the Park for passholders tonight, in advance of the event's official opening tomorrow. Four themed areas take over the front half of the New Jersey park, including Glittering Gateway, Santa's Arctic North Pole, Sweet Street, and Coastal Christmas. Entertainment includes Holiday Road � Live on Tour, Glistening Snow Show and Lights! Magic! Christmas!

For our complete list of ongoing and upcoming events at theme parks this year and next, please visit themeparkinsider.com/calendar.

title: Universal files plan for self-fixing theme park attraction
summary:
By Robert Niles: Theme park fans who have spent a lot of time in the parks know that many attractions have what's called a "B" mode.

A B mode is when an effect or element of a theme park attraction is not working properly, so the attraction's ride or show system switches to an alternative. In some cases, for an example, an animatronic fails, so a screen shows the character instead.

How an attraction switches from normal operation ("A" mode) to B mode depends on the specific ride or show. Sometimes, that's a decision for third-shift maintenance and others, it's something that ride ops can control. Now, Universal has plans for a more robust system for switching theme park attractions into B mode.

In a new patent application published today, Universal describes its plans for how attractions can switch into one of a variety of potential alternate operations on the fly, based on current ride and show conditions. The application is called "Systems and Methods for Operating an Amusement Park System."

(Systems for a system? Ah, the joy of writing - and reading - legalese.)

If one prop is misplaced, perhaps the ride adjusts its path to avoid it. Or if a prop is not fulfilling its programmed function, another prop can be called into action to take that role. The proposed system could use machine learning to fine-tune its repertoire of adjustments.

To use a sports analogy, it's like having a coach on the sidelines that can make calls and substitutions to keep the team competitive. Ultimately, the goal here is uptime while providing guests with an experience that comes as close to what designers intended as possible.

You can read Universal's full application here: Systems and Methods for Operating an Amusement Park System.

title: Disney has a plan to make moving chocolate treats
summary:
By Robert Niles: It's usually not good when a treat you're about to eat starts moving. Human beings have not evolved to eat live things. When we see food that's moving, well, we tend to assume that something's alive in there and... that ain't good.

But what if that piece of food only created the illusion of movement? What if that bite was shaped in a way that it formed a holographic image on its surface? That way, the food might look like some enchanted or otherworldly consumable that would fit right in at, oh say, a theme park.

In a new patent application published this week, Disney offers its plan for creating holograms on food, using microscopic physical textures molded into its surface. The idea is that the texture would interact with light so that a consumer would see what looked like a moving holographic image on the food item.

As someone who handles all the cooking and baking in my home, this one absolutely blows my mind. Have you ever tempered chocolate before? Getting that stuff to behave and hold the shape you want is a bit of a trick. Doing that at a microscopic level that would allow you to design a hologram on a piece of chocolate demands a level of industrial baking and confectionery work that's simply beyond the comprehension of a home cook.

But building something like Rise of the Resistance lies far beyond the comprehension of anyone creating home haunts and backyard fairs, so I guess that this tracks for Disney.

The trick here seems to be the design of the mold and then preparing the food that goes into that mold to be able to hold the mold's microscopic design. This is why the term "food science" exists, and Disney acknowledges that specific confections may require the addition of fats, sugars or other ingredients in order to make the process work and produce the texture needed for the hologram to work.

So where might we see such confections in the park? Well, monsters eat moving things, so my first guess would be some new sweet treats in Walt Disney World's upcoming Monstropolis land. But there likely are abundant applications for such effects in the Marvel universe, as well.

If you want to get into all the details, you can read Disney's proposal here: Microscopic Physical Textures for Confections.

title: Disney World's Pirates to get Thunder-style refurb
summary:
By Robert Niles: Drink up, me hearties, for it's about to be last call on Pirates of the Caribbean at Walt Disney World - at least for a while.

Disney announced this morning that the Magic Kingdom's Pirates of the Caribbean will go down for refurbishment starting January 11, 2027. Disney is planning a Thunder Mountain-style refresh of the attraction, with a planned return later in 2027.

During the refurbishment, Disney's Imagineers will be making thematic additions and enhancements to the long-running attraction, in addition to Disney performing basic maintenance and ride system upgrades.

Theme Park Insider readers are voting now for their favorite attractions around the world, but I don't think that I am spoiling anything by suggesting that Florida's Pirates rides once again will end up the lowest-rated of Disney's Pirates of the Caribbean attractions worldwide. This one needs some love, and - as a former Pirates of the Caribbean attractions cast member in Florida - I am happy to hear that the attraction will be getting that.

So in case you can't get to Orlando for one last ride on the current version before it goes down, here is my ride-through POV video of the WDW Pirates.

For more theme park news, please sign up for Theme Park Insider's free weekly newsletter.

title: Universal Orlando to open Epic Universal to annual passes
summary:
By Robert Niles: It's happening. Universal Orlando soon will open its new Epic Universe theme park to annual passholders.

Don't fire up the car and head over just yet, though. Current Universal Orlando Annual Pass holders will need to upgrade the passes in order to visit Epic Universe. Then, once they do so, they will need to make a reservation to use their upgraded UOAP to visit the park.

That's right. Park reservations are back on the east coast. Disneyland Magic Key holders have been doing pass reservations for years in California. Universal Orlando Annual Passholders soon will be joining them, at least when they want to visit Epic. Reservations will not be required at the other parks.

Oh, and by the way, they're not going to be "Annual Passholders" at Universal Orlando anymore. When Universal introduces its new annual pass program starting next month, the resort will start calling the people who buy those passes "Pass Members."

In addition, the names of Universal's pass tiers will be changing:

  • Premier will become Platinum,
  • Preferred will become Gold,
  • Power will become Silver,
  • Seasonal will become Bronze.

This brings Orlando in line with the vocabulary now used at Universal Studios Hollywood. Consider this the policy to be named later in the deal a few years back that forced USH to start calling its Halloween Horror Nights mazes "houses" to match Orlando.

If that's not enough change for you, yep, there's more. Universal Orlando will phasing out plastic-card annual passes, switching to digital passes in the Universal Orlando app. Let's see y'all start wearing your phones on those lanyards now.

The Epic Universe upgrades will be available to current eligible UOAP "members" starting next month. The Florida resident price for the upgrade will range from $125 to $410, depending upon your current pass level. Pass members not in their upgrade window will get prorated prices for the upgrade, depending upon pass level and how much time remains on their pass.

Once they upgrade, pass members may make reservations to visit Epic starting January 4, 2027. Pass members may hold up to two reservations at a time. Reservation availability will be limited, as Universal looks to continue limiting access to Epic Universe.

The reservation requirement seems to me a fair trade-off to allow pass members access to the park while Universal tries to protect Epic's day ticket buyers from being stuck in endless queues behind annual passholders.

The upgrade opportunity will roll out in phases by pass level, starting next month. All current passholders will have the opportunity to upgrade (and make reservations) before the new Epic Universe-inclusive annual passes go on sale to the public later in December. Epic Universe-inclusive Passes will start at $449.99, for Florida residents.

Stay tuned for additional details, including program start dates and other price points. To keep up with more theme park news, please sign up for Theme Park Insider's free weekly newsletter.

title: United Parks offers fresh looks at what's next in 2027
summary:
By Robert Niles: United Parks threw a bit of a coming-out party at the IAAPA Expo today for its United Parks Creative team. The company has launched new social media channels for its attraction design shop, which was known as Deep Blue Creative back when the company was called SeaWorld Parks and Entertainment.

I posted earlier about the company's new launched water coaster coming to Busch Gardens Tampa Bay next summer: Busch Gardens is getting a new water coaster for 2027. United Parks today also offered fresh looks at two previously announced attractions coming to its parks.

SEAQuest: Legends of the Deep

First announced in 2025 for debut this year, then delayed, this Vekoma suspended dark ride now is scheduled to open next year at SeaWorld Orlando.

United Parks Creative today shared a couple of pieces of concept art for the ride, which will take riders on a simulated undersea adventure on free swinging ride vehicles that can rotate 360 degrees.


Images courtesy United Parks


Finding treasure on SEAQuest: Legends of the Deep

Return to Corkscrew Hill

This Brogent Technologies motion ride will open next year at Busch Gardens Williamsburg. The show calls back to the Corkscrew Hill motion theater show that ran at the park from 2001 to 2010.

Here's the set-up from United Parks Creative: "Guests are invited to McLarney Castle for an exhibition on Irish myths and folklore. The witch Moll lures them into an off-limits gallery, where an enchanted painting transports them into the world of Corkscrew Hill. Friendly fairies explain that the only way home is through another enchanted painting in Moll�s tower."


The witch Moll. Images courtesy United Parks


Inside the queue

Stay tuned for specific opening dates. For more theme park news, please sign up for Theme Park Insider's free weekly newsletter.

title: Busch Gardens is getting a new water coaster for 2027, too
summary:
By Robert Niles: Did you like yesterday's Mack Rides water coaster announcement at the IAAPA Expo in Orlando?

If you did, here's treat for you - a second Mack Rides water coaster announcement, today!

One day after Mack Rides and Holiday World revealed one of the ride vehicles for the Cannonball! water coaster coming next year to the Santa Claus, Indiana theme park, United Parks announced that it will be bringing a water coaster to Busch Gardens Tampa Bay in 2027.

Simbi Rush will be the first launched water coaster in North America and the fastest water coaster on the continent, the park said in its announcement. (I am guessing that means Mack Rides water coasters, and that we're not counting the Intamin launched flume ride at SeaWorld San Antonio here.)

Simbi Rush will feature a top speed 40 mph with two launches and a story inspired by Central African folklore about water guardian spirits. The ride is going in on the site of the former Stanley Falls Flume and will open next summer. Here is the reveal video from the park.

What's the over/under on the percentage of fans who end up calling this Simba Rush, after The Lion King protagonist?
